newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania plans new 1997-2000 privatisation wave.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania plans new 1997-2000 privatisation wave.

text.p: The Lithuanian government on Friday said it would soon approve a new list of key companies for sale.
The list would include companies in sectors which until now have been banned from privatisation, such as the energy, communications and transport.

"In the near future, a government meeting will approve a list of the country's most important energy, communications, transport and other companies to be privatised over the years 1997-2000," the government press office said in a statement.
The government intends to suggest that laws which ban the sale of companies considered strategic and not allowed for sale until 2000 should be declared "null and void", the office said.
Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius, who leads a right-wing coalition that ousted former Communists in November 1996 elections, has pledged to speed economic reform and privatisation.
Lithuania has gained the reputation of being a laggard in the race to reform and has attracted less foreign investment than its Baltic neighbours Latvia and Estonia.
Companies so far considered as strategic include the national airline Lithuanian Airlines, Lithuanian Telecommunications, the railways and ports.
The government said the privatisations would be carried out via open international tenders.
The bids would be announced by the shareholders of the firms with the privatisation agency, which would organise the privatisation programmes and the search for investors.
